title: The French Revolution - OverSimplified (Part 1)
subject: History
beats: Cold open: a royal wedding party; 'France is in financial ruin' set up as a running gag
France as glorious, with an aside: who cares about the starving 80%?
France as a little buddy goes to war with Britain and loses; debt
Party harder; peasants pick up the slack, as society has accepted for centuries
A peasant asks why: why nobles, why a king? That's the Enlightenment
Louis becomes king: sum-up of debt and doubt; catchphrase scream
Louis XVI: weak and easily manipulated
Funds the American revolution; America walks away from the loan
Marie Antoinette's spending, 'Madame Deficit', scandal pamphlets
Skit: tax collectors tax windows, tithe, salt, a crying child
Harvest share, labor tax, inconsistency, tax-free first two estates
What could push them over the edge? Bad harvests, bread prices, riots
King summons the Estates General, unused for 175 years; three estates
Porsches for clergy and nobility, nothing for France's debt
Voting: 130,000 people, one vote; 350,000, one vote; 27 million, one vote
Every motion passes two to one against the third estate
Third estate forms the National Assembly
Locked out, they find a tennis court: the Tennis Court Oath
Introduces Robespierre, Danton and the Jacobins, who want the king gone
Fear on every side: king fears the people, people fear the army
National Guard forms; Invalides raided for rifles but no powder
Storming the Bastille; the king in denial at the governor's head on a pike
The Assembly had two options and embraced the violence; some historians see the roots of the bloodshed here
Marat writes 'kill them all' from his bathtub, then coos at a rubber duck
Declaration of the Rights of Man: landmark, but only for men
People cared more about bread; the king lived far away at Versailles
Women's march on Versailles; 'let them eat cake' played as a gag
Palace broken into; king agrees to share power and move to Paris

meta.notation_note: No notation. New terms (estates, Estates General, National Assembly, Jacobins) are introduced as characters or skits.
meta.misconception: partial: 1:44 glamorous France undercut by sarcasm; 15:18 'let them eat cake' shown as a gag, not as fact-checked
meta.examples: skits: tax collector, voting, Bastille, march on Versailles
